DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 74 s. 2021 07 June 2021 HON. PEDRO B. BELARMINO Vice-Mayor Sangguniang Bayan of Caoayan Ilocos Sur Dear Vice-Mayor Belarmino: This has reference to your letter dated 22 February 2021 requesting this Department's legal opinion concerning the penalty of SB Caoayan ordinance on the mandatory wearing of facemask by all persons in public places. Per your letter, on 3 August 2020, the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) of Caoayan, Ilocos Sur enacted Ordinance No. 20-04 entitled "An Ordinance Requiring the Mandatory Wearing of Facemasks by all Persons in the Public Places within the Territorial Jurisdiction of the Municipality of Caoayan, Ilocos Sur as Precautionary Measure to Prevent the Transmission/spread of the Corona Virus Disease (COVID-19)". Said Ordinance was approved by Municipal Mayor Germelina S. Goulart on 10 August 2020. Section 5 of the subject Ordinance provides for the penalty/ies for violations thereof. It states that any person who violates the provisions Of this ordinance shall be penalized with the following: 1. FirstOffense- Fine of Five Hundred Pesos (P500.OO) or imprisonment of one (1) day; and 2. Second Offense- Fine of One Thousand Pesos (PIOOO.OO) or imprisonment of two (2) days. On 3 September 2020, the subject Ordinance was received by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Ilocos Sur for its review and approval pursuant to Section 468 (1 ) (i) of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991. Subsequently, in a report dated 2 October 2020, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Ilocos Sur, Committee on Review of Municipal Statutes

found that the subject Ordinance was non-compliant with Inter-Agency Task Force (IATF) Omnibus Guidelines on the Implementation of Community Quarantine in the Philippines which provides for a higher penalties for the violation of mandatory wearing of facemask. Relatively, this Department, in conformity with the IATF Omnibus Guidelines and minimum public health standards prescribed by Department of Health, issued several memorandum circulars urging the local government units to enact or amend existing local ordinances to include penal provisions strengthening the implementation of quarantine, health and safety standard protocols to contain COVID-19. Corollarilyy this Department recommends the following penalties for people who violate the mandatory wearing of facemasks in public spaces, thus: Fine ranging from Php2,500.00- Php5,000.00 1. Province- and/or imprisonment for 10-30 days at the discretion of proper court; Fine ranging from Php2,500.00- Php5,000.00 2. City- and/or imprisonment for 10-30 days at the discretion of proper court; and 3. Municipality- Fine ranging from Phpl ,OOO.OO- Php2,500.OO and/or imprisonment for 10-30 days at the discretion of proper court, As a matter of compliance, herein concerned SB amended the subject Ordinance by virtue of Ordinance No. 20-08 on 23 November 2020 with the following penalty clause, to wit: "Section 5. PENALTY- Any person who violates the provisions of this ordinance shall be penalized with the following: 1. First Offense- Fine of One Thousand Pesos (PI ,OOO.OO) or imprisonment of five (5) days; 2. Second Offense- Fine of One Thousand Five Hundred Pesos (Pl ,500) or imprisonment for seven (7) days; AND 3. Third Offense- Fine of Two Thousand Five Hundred Pesos or imprisonment of ten 10 (days)." However, the foregoing was subsequently vetoed by your Municipal Mayor as the new penalties are higher compared to Ordinance No. 20-04,

Hence, your request for legal opinion. At the outset, this Department is of the view that insofar as the violation of local ordinance is concerned, local government units are guided by the Local Government Code of 1991 (Code). Specifically; in the case of sangguniang bayan, Sections 447 (a) (1) (iii) of the Code provides, viz: The sangguniang bayan, as the legislative body of the municipality, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general' welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the municipality as provided for under Section 22 of this Godey and shall; (I ) Approve ordinances and pass resolutions necessary for an efficient and effective municipal government, and in this connection shall: (iii) Approve ordinances imposing a fine not exceeding Two thousand five hundred pesos (P2,500.OO) or an imprisonment for a period not exceeding six (6) months, or both in the discretion of the court, for the violation of a municipal ordinance. Let it be emphasized that the aforesaid DILG issuance, which provides for stiffer penalties than that of the subject Ordinance is in line with the aforequoted provision of the Local Government Code. Along this line, it may be well to take into account the legal weight of an IATF guidelines. This Department holds the view that IATF issuances/guidelines are mere recommendatory in nature— and not mandatory. Stated otherwise, a guideline, or an IATF guidelinefor that matter, is not a law. Further, generally, a guidelines do not have penal provisions, while ordinance has. Notwithstanding, in light of the unabated increase of COVID-19 cases in the country, this Department, in view of its supervisory functions over local government units, reiterates its Memorandum Circular for local government units to adopt a stiffer penalty/ies in their local ordinances strengthening the implementation of health and safety standard protocols to contain COVID- 19.

This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, UTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ANS CESO Ill Undersec tary for Local Government LLLS/27 Copy fumished: DIR. JAMES F.
